posts.text: The options market post Warsh. The lean into a bullish/call stance in both bond ETFs and equities has faded. Points moving toward put skew. This reads more disappointment vs fear.
Lots of positive gamma support today for SPX and from aggregate single stocks. Dealers should buy dips.
Institutional investors are extremely bullish worldwide. Long positioning in S&P 500 futures among asset managers is up to ~$375 billion, near its highest level on record.
Bullish positioning in gold is surging. Call minus put OI on GLD hit ~2.4 million contracts, highest since February. Macro and currency uncertainty driving bets on gold.
JPMorgan strategist Jason Hunter flagged growing risks of a late-summer or early-autumn market downturn despite major indexes remaining in bullish trends.
After Cruel Summer for bonds, Citadel Securities macro maven flips bullish on duration.
Spain CPI (Y/Y) Aug P: 4.3% (est 4.2%; prev 3.6%) — hotter inflation print in Europe.
FRANCE (AUG) CPI Y/Y ACTUAL: 2.4% VS 2.1% PREVIOUS; EST. 2.4%. Harmonized slightly hot.
Warsh Jackson Hole: underlying trends have not meaningfully improved. Bond market heard hike risk — Sep 15-16 odds ~55-60%.
Rates first, stocks second. Friday NFP will move September hike odds more than any single earnings print. VIX still near year lows.
S&P roughly 1.1% off the Aug 13 high. Big-cap tech held the tape; small caps did not. Volume light, VIX near the year's lows.
Policy rate 3.50-3.75%. After Warsh, futures pricing ~55-60% chance of a 25bp hike on Sep 15-16. That is the week's frame into NFP.
